question: How many of the world's one-year-olds today have been vaccinated against some disease?
answer: About 80 percent. Rosling asked this across many countries, and most people guessed far lower. Vaccines need cold storage and working health systems, so a high number means most of the world has them, which is exactly what our picture of the world leaves out.
move: The quiet systems that work rarely make the news, so you guess them too low.
trap: 20 percent: the picture of a world mostly without basic care.
simply: Most babies in the world get their vaccine jabs. You just never see a news story saying 'baby gets jab, is fine'.
why: Underrating what already works makes every problem look hopeless and every solution look pointless.
